blocks.text:
Goals
Goals
• Simulate a methane/air flame in a microgravity environment
and with the application of an electric field.
Create a chemical kinetic mechanism for methane/air
flames including ions and excited species suitable for
inclusion in CFD models.
Examine this new mechanism for non-premixed
methane/air flames using OpenFOAM® and
CHEMKIN® software.
Try new approaches to reach accurate simulations
(Lower Mach Number code with Adaptive Mesh
Resolution; LBNL)
ASGSR. 32nd Annual Meeting. Oct. 26-29, 2016 7

boundary condition.

blocks.text:
LBNL Research
Parallel research
Simulations with Lower Mach Number code with Adaptive Mesh Refinement
Basic idea
Governing equations can be solved, at each time-step, on a multilevel grid.
Main advantages
• Mesh is refined only where it is needed saves time and computational
costs
• LMN code VS Constant Density Projection bigger steps and more robust
so it can perform AMR
Temperature profile [K] for a 2D co-flow diffusion flame
Work in progress by Valentina Ricchiuti (Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, CA)
ASGSR. 32nd Annual Meeting. Oct. 26-29, 2016 18

blocks.text:
Summary
Summary
• A preliminary model for non-premixed methane/air
flames that contains both chemi-ions and excited
species has been achieved.
• 2D simulations have to be done to check CH* and OH*
concentrations with experiments.
• LBNL Adaptative Mesh Refinement (AMR) has been
successfully implemented in 1D simulations with e-field
applied.
• LBNL – AMR technique should be improved to apply it
in 2D simulations with e-field.
ASGSR. 32nd Annual Meeting. Oct. 26-29, 2016 19
